behavioral_notes.observation: _compute_access_url returns '#' by default and is overridden on each business document (sale.order, account.move, ...). _portal_ensure_token lazily mints a uuid4 access_token via a sudo write (forcing cache clear), and get_portal_url / _get_share_url append '?access_token=...' so an emailed link bypasses the recipient's ACLs. Not visible in metadata.

Controller helper used by every /my/* document route: tries document.check_access('read'); on AccessError it falls back to a constant-time consteq(access_token) comparison against the record's signed token, returning the SUDOED record. This is the mechanism that lets unauthenticated/public visitors view a shared document without backend rights.

_sign_token builds an HMAC-SHA256 of (dbname, access_token, pid) keyed by ir.config_parameter 'database.secret', so an emailed recipient identified by pid+hash can post in the portal chatter as a known author. _notify_get_recipients_groups injects a 'portal_customer' button-access link; website_message_ids exposes the public (comment/email) communication history on any portal.mixin record.

Provisions external access: if the partner has no user it creates a res.users via _create_user_from_template, then writes group_ids += base.group_portal and -= base.group_public, runs signup_prepare() and sends the auth_signup.portal_set_password_email invitation. Revoke archives the user (active=False) but keeps it in group_portal. These side-effects (user creation, group membership, signup mail) are pure Python, invisible to metadata.

27 JS files, 6 XML templates, 2 OWL components (PortalChatter, SignatureForm); 11 registry registrations and 7 patches of core web/mail prototypes (Chatter, Composer, Message, Thread, AttachmentUploadService, SuggestionService, chatHubService). Dedicated frontend chatter bundles (portal.assets_chatter*, 21 files each) re-host the backend mail chatter inside the public /my surface.

information_flows: depends: web, html_editor, http_routing, mail, auth_signup
side-effect: portal.wizard.user.action_grant_access -> res.users + base.group_portal + signup email
side-effect: portal.share.action_send_mail -> mail.message (share link) on the target document
side-effect: portal.mixin._portal_ensure_token -> signed access_token bypassing recipient ACLs

value_streams: Invite-to-Self-Service: grant portal access -> signup email -> customer logs in to /my -> views shared documents & posts in chatter
policies: 3 ACL rows scope portal.share / portal.wizard(.user) to base.group_partner_manager (no unlink)
token policy: consteq(access_token) + HMAC(dbname, token, pid) keyed by database.secret gate public document & chatter access
portal.allow_api_keys config flag toggles whether portal users may create API keys

classification.rationale: portal is a mediating (network) value model: it provides the infrastructure that connects external customers to the organisation's documents and conversations, with no production of its own. It is model-light / route-heavy (4 own models vs 18 /my/* routes) — a web access surface rather than a transactional engine. As an enabler it is a support activity that provisions and secures the self-service channel; its closest APQC anchor is 6.0 Manage Customer Service (post-order self-service / inquiry handling, cf. apqc 3.5.4.8). The mediation is realised through portal.mixin's signed access tokens, the portal.wizard user-provisioning flow, and the shared portal chatter.

standard_capabilities: self-service portal dashboard (/my) with per-app document counters
grant/revoke portal access wizard (auto-creates res.users + signup email)
signed-token document sharing & 'Share' action on any portal.mixin record
password change, account deactivation, optional API-key management
portal chatter (post & read messages on shared documents)
typical_fits: B2B/B2C customers viewing their own quotations/orders/invoices online
contact manager inviting partners to the portal in batch
emailed share links that authenticate the recipient into the document chatter
common_gaps: branding/theming of /my pages (usually needs website + custom QWeb)
exposing additional document types (each needs its own controller + portal.mixin mixin-in)
custom self-service workflows beyond view/comment (e.g. portal-side approvals)
fine-grained per-document visibility beyond owner + access_token
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['portal.wizard'].create({}).user_ids — inspect computed portal user states

curl -s '<base>/my' (expects redirect to /web/login when unauthenticated; auth=user)
curl jsonrpc /my/counters with a portal user session to fetch badge counts
